research_question: Can increasingly explicit semantic-preservation structure reduce mechanism-to-CodeQL translation loss while retaining compilability?

T0_original_mechanism_first_translation.important_caveat: The single strict hit-based success was semantically wrong under the frozen human mechanism review.

main_findings: Mechanism-first planning represented 6/7 actual mechanisms, yet all three translation variants retained 0/7 semantic alignment.
Prompt-only semantic-preservation instructions did not reduce the observed 6/7 plan-to-CodeQL translation loss.
Structured mechanism contracts also did not reduce semantic loss, but they made failure more explicit by marking 2/3 mechanism families UNENCODABLE_OR_BOUNDED.
Matched V3 repair recovered compilation from 0/7 to 7/7 for T2, but semantic alignment remained 0/7 and all seven cases were detection failures.
The dominant observed bottleneck in this CWE-639 TRAIN pilot is preserving decisive security relations during mechanism unification and CodeQL translation, not compilation alone.
next_research_implication: The next intervention should test compositional translation: generate mechanism-specific CodeQL branches or sub-predicates independently, verify each branch against its structured semantic contract, and only then unify them into the required single CWE-level query.
limitations: Evidence is restricted to seven CWE-639 TRAIN pairs.
No cross-CWE generalization claim is made.
Failure-transparency improvement is diagnostic, not a semantic-accuracy improvement.
